text:
Minnesota and Montreal arrive hot. The Wild have points in eight straight (6-0-2) but just saw a three-game winning streak end when Tampa Bay came back from two goals down to win 4-3 in overtime. They're without Jared Spurgeon. The Canadiens have points in ten straight (8-0-2), most recently a 4-2 win in Toronto, and they're missing Ivan Demidov and Mike Matheson, with ESPN's estimated return for both on Nov 14. Cole Caufield has moved onto Juraj Slafkovský's line, and Kaiden Guhle is up to 24:46 a night.

Our numbers see little between them. At five on five, MIN has 53% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) and MTL 52%, and we have the Wild 3.32 to 2.90 tonight. The matchup to watch is Minnesota's power play, at 0.95 expected goals a game, against Montreal's penalty kill, which allows 0.90. The Canadiens take 5.2 penalties a game. In net, projected starters Jesper Wallstedt (+13.3 goals saved above expected, how many goals a goalie has stopped beyond what the shots predicted) and Jacob Fowler (+11.2) are both on heaters, though Wallstedt's 5.76 last season trails Fowler's 5.98 in a bigger sample.

Kirill Kaprizov, on an eight-game point streak, is our top scoring pick at 48%, with Matt Boldy at 40%. For Montreal, Caufield leads at 37% and Slafkovský plays his 300th game. Our under-the-radar pick is Minnesota's Bobby Brink, a third-liner at 14:30 a night with 2.2 expected goals over his last 10 games. We have him at 16% to score, a player to watch, not a lock.
